caption:
5 Bali temples built by the sea. Save this for your trip.

05 Pura Sakenan: once reached on foot at low tide
04 Goa Lawah: home to thousands of bats
03 Rambut Siwi: the temple of a holy lock of hair
02 Tanah Lot: “land in the sea”
01 Uluwatu: about 70 metres above the waves

Number 1 is ten minutes from Yume by Nyara, our three private-pool villas above Bingin. Link in bio to book your stay in Bali.

slides.sub: Number 1 stands on a cliff about 70 metres above the waves.

slides.label: 05 · Pura Sakenan, Serangan
slides.answer: On foot at low tide, by boat at high.
slides.body: The great festival here falls on Kuningan, every 210 days. Its oldest shrines were built from limestone and coral.

slides.label: 04 · Goa Lawah, Klungkung
slides.body: Goa Lawah means “bat cave”. The temple is built around its mouth, and legend says the cave runs right through the mountain.

slides.label: 03 · Rambut Siwi, Jembrana
slides.body: Rambut Siwi means “venerated hair”. Legend says the priest Nirartha left a lock of his here, and the fallen walls rose again.

slides.label: 02 · Tanah Lot, Tabanan
slides.body: Tanah Lot sits on a rock in the surf. At low tide you can walk towards it, and legend says sea snakes guard its base.

slides.label: 01 · Uluwatu, the Bukit
slides.body: Pura Luhur Uluwatu crowns a cliff at the Bukit's south-western tip, one of Bali's directional temples. Ten minutes from Bingin.

slides.credit: Villa Tiga, Yume by Nyara, Bingin
slides.eyebrow: Now you know where to watch the sunset
slides.body: Three private-pool villas on the clifftops of Bingin, ten minutes from Uluwatu Temple. From USD 135 a night.
